reveal.terms: "Indexing" means writing a name in filing order: surname first, then given name, then middle initial. A title such as Dr. is the last unit.
reveal.shortcut: Rewrite each surname as one block: drop spaces and hyphens, keep the prefix (Dela Cruz = DELACRUZ). Then compare letter by letter (ARMA Rule 1). Order: Teresita M. De los Santos → DELOSSANTOS, Teresita; Maria B. Dizon → DIZON, Maria; Imelda N. Manalo → MANALO, Imelda; Andres D. Navarro → NAVARRO, Andres.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: "Teresita M. De los Santos". Index each name surname first, letter by letter: DELOSSANTOS, DIZON, MANALASTAS, VILLANUEVA. "De" comes before "Di", so De los Santos files first. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 6), not a rule published by the CSC. Source standard: ANSI/ARMA 12-2005.

why_wrong.o1: "Imelda N. Manalastas" files as MANALASTAS, which comes after DELOSSANTOS.
why_wrong.o3: "Andres D. Villanueva" is first only if you sort by the given name. Personal names file by surname first: VILLANUEVA is last.
why_wrong.o4: "Rosalinda B. Dizon" is first only if the prefix of De los Santos is filed as a separate word. A prefix joins the rest of the surname: DELOSSANTOS comes before DIZON.

Investigate human rights violations and monitor compliance

reveal.terms: 1987 Constitution: Art. II principles and state policies, Art. III Bill of Rights, Art. IV citizenship, Art. VIII judiciary, Art. XIII Secs. 17-19 Commission on Human Rights.
reveal.shortcut: The CHR investigates and monitors; courts try and convict; Congress makes laws.
